Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )$ for $\frac{\pi }{8}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{8},$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )$, ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{\pi }{8}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{3\pi }{8}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /8}^{3\pi /8}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{\pi /8}^{3\pi /8}{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /8}^{3\pi /8}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\theta \,{|}_{\pi /8}^{3\pi /8}+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta )\,{|}_{\pi /8}^{3\pi /8} \\  & =(\frac{3\pi }{8}-\frac{\pi }{8})+\frac{1}{8}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}+0 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
